paragraphs: Children in care in Bridgend County Borough are looked after by Foster Wales Bridgend, the council's own fostering service, and by the agencies listed on this page. In March 2025 the council said more foster carers were needed locally: the number of children in foster care had stayed broadly the same in recent years, but the number of carers available had fallen. The council has said that placing children with carers inside the county borough helps them keep the same school, health care, friends and family contact, and that in the previous year 85 per cent of young people with its own carers stayed in their area.

Foster Wales Bridgend says it does not make a profit from children in care and reinvests its funding in its service and carers. It says some of its carers receive between £12,782 and £43,056 a year, depending on how many children they look after and what kind of fostering they do. Its carers have a network of more than 70 local foster carers, with experienced liaison carers acting as mentors, support 24 hours a day, therapeutic advice, training, and free leisure membership for the household.

Bridgend is part of the Welsh Government's move away from profit-making care: from 1 April 2026 new fostering providers in Wales must be not-for-profit. Talk to the council and one or two of the agencies below, and compare training, support and pay before you apply.
